name: zap-018b9139-blind28-ots
instr:
# uber-go/zap: wrong output, inverted filtering and silent mis-parsing, diagnosed without a test suite

An application built on this library keeps a structured account of what it does: it decides what is worth keeping, attaches data to each entry, turns entries into bytes and hands those bytes to one or more destinations. Every one of those steps now produces wrong results somewhere. Nothing about the callers changed, and calls that used to behave correctly no longer do; in several places something that used to be rejected is quietly accepted, and something that used to be accepted is refused. The repository has received 28 separate undocumented edits.

Deciding what is worth keeping goes wrong from the start. Turning the word "debug" into a mutable severity holder gives back a holder that still sits at info, and handing the same conversion the word "FOO" returns quietly with no complaint at all about the unrecognized word; only asking for "info" happens to land on the right answer. Reading such a holder back from text shows the same shape of trouble: after reading the word for warning, the word for failure or the word for fatal, the threshold is still info, and reading "foobar" is accepted without complaint, although turning a threshold that was set programmatically back into text still produces the right word. Restricting a destination that already accepts info and above so that it accepts only debug and above should be refused as a contradiction, but it now hands back a us
